findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike `disconnectMutation` below it, it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The `cacheUpdatedAt` value that drives the 'Cache Status' section and the 'Delete cached data' item comes from that query. When `onChanged` is not passed by the parent (it is optional in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`), the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp and a delete action for cache that no longer exists after a successful delete. Add an `onSettled`/`onSuccess` invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

findings.title: Extra updateMany on SelectedCalendar on every cache refresh with no consumer
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache population (called from every Google webhook and from unwatch). The PR description itself admits `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not displayed anywhere; the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This adds a write touching every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on each webhook purely as a side effect, with no functional purpose, and bumps `updatedAt` on rows that did not semantically change. It also relies on Prisma applying `@updatedAt` with an empty `data` object, which is implicit behaviour. This should be removed.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars but nothing in this module uses them
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, yet `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` and its helpers never read either field. This tightens the public contract of `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` (re-exported as a legacy export for `@calcom/platform-libraries` / API v2 consumers) and forces every caller that builds a `UserWithCalendars` from a narrower Prisma select to add these columns or fail type-checking. Only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated here; other callers (platform API, tests) are at risk of breaking for no benefit. Revert the type change or justify the fields.

findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError, surfacing as 500 for not-found/forbidden credential
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps generic errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) and logs them as server failures, whereas this is a client-side condition. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `FORBIDDEN`) so the client gets a meaningful status and the error is not reported as a server bug.

findings.title: CalendarCacheRepository instantiated directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag
findings.body: The handler does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which selects the mock repository when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. The newly added `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` mock exists precisely for that case but is never reachable from this path, so a DB `groupBy` query is executed on every connectedCalendars load even for deployments/teams where caching is off.

findings.title: Script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and cwd-relative .env path
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU sed (Linux) `''` is treated as the input file name and the command fails with "can't read : No such file". Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running it from the repo root creates/edits a `.env` one directory above the repo. Use a portable in-place edit (e.g. write to a temp file) and derive the path from `$(dirname "$0")`.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US locale, ignoring user locale/time format
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is used to render the 'Last updated' timestamp even though the component already has `useLocale()`. Users with other locales or 24h time format preferences will see US-formatted dates/times inconsistent with the rest of the app. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale()` / `i18n.language`) or the existing dayjs helpers.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` while `tsx` is not listed in dependencies or devDependencies (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will attempt to download the latest `tsx` from the registry at runtime, which is non-reproducible, requires network access, and prompts interactively in some npm versions. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep using the installed `ts-node`.
